children.label: a
children.prompt: Find all integer solutions of the equation $xy+2x+3y=8$ by first writing it in the form $(x+a)(y+b)=c$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}xy+2x+3y&=8\\xy+2x+3y+6&=14\\x(y+2)+3(y+2)&=14\\(x+3)(y+2)&=14\end{align*}$$
Thus $a=3$, $b=2$ and $c=14$.

The complete list of ordered integer factor pairs is
$$\begin{aligned}(x+3,y+2)\in\{&(1,14),(2,7),(7,2),(14,1),\\&(-1,-14),(-2,-7),(-7,-2),(-14,-1)\}.\end{aligned}$$
Subtracting $3$ from each first coordinate and $2$ from each second coordinate gives
$$\begin{aligned}(x,y)\in\{&(-2,12),(-1,5),(4,0),(11,-1),\\&(-4,-16),(-5,-9),(-10,-4),(-17,-3)\}.\end{aligned}$$
These are all the solutions because every ordered integer factor pair of $14$ has been included.

Factorise to $(x+2)(y-5)=11$ and use every signed integer factor pair of $11$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}xy-5x+2y&=21\\xy-5x+2y-10&=11\\x(y-5)+2(y-5)&=11\\(x+2)(y-5)&=11\end{align*}$$
Since $11$ is prime, all ordered integer factor pairs are
$$(x+2,y-5)\in\{(1,11),(11,1),(-1,-11),(-11,-1)\}.$$
Subtracting $2$ from each first coordinate and adding $5$ to each second coordinate gives
$$(x,y)\in\{(-1,16),(9,6),(-3,-6),(-13,4)\}.$$
These exhaust all signed integer factor pairs, so there are no other integer solutions.
